top_signal.title: Trading a government desk job for a rural retreat business: feasibility check on a boutique workshop & rental concept
top_signal.summary: TL;DR Planning to leave my stable job over the next few years and trade city life for a life close to nature with my husband and future family. The vision is an intimate rural property (where I live) with a studio for hand-crafted nature workshops led by local makers and a single eco-cabin for short-term guests. Seeking practical advice on the operational and management realities of running this model.  ------   Hey everyone, so first things first, I've never made a post like this before, so sorry if it's a bit all over the place or doesn't follow the right format. I will receive any feedback with humility!   I’m planning an exit strategy from my public service desk job here in Ontario, Canada, in hopes of having a lifestyle that is closer to nature and more creative. I know whatever I do will likely earn less than I'm currently making and have less stability, but it's more about having a lifestyle that feels true to me. My husband and I want to move to the country, start a family, and he will commute to his job (hybrid) in the city. My goal is to be able to stay home with the kids while running this business, scaling it up over time. I dream of getting away from the city noise and pollution and just being near trees, wildlife, open skies, etc. My husband actually just completed an MBA while working as an engineer, so I would have a lot of help with the backend of the business.
